title: The Overview Room
subtitle: Your life, seen from above. Things you didn't know you missed.

customObject.name: the life-map table
customObject.description: a wide table rendering a man's forty years as terrain seen from altitude — a ravine through the middle years, and threads of light the ground never showed him

script.note: A dark room with a wide, lit table. A man stands over it with a departure form folded in his pocket. He filed it yesterday: permanent.

script.text: Good evening, Nils. You're leaving us — the Threshold flagged your filing, and departures are offered this room. Not to argue with you. The map doesn't argue. It only shows altitude.
I know how it works. Astronauts look down at the whole Earth at once and come back different — the overview effect. You do it to a life instead. My Lantern's been suggesting it for a year.

Then you know the rule of instruments here: I add nothing. Every light on this table is a real event, consented to by the other person in it. I can't flatter you. I can only stop you seeing your life from inside your own weather. Shall we climb?

script.note: The table breathes out. Forty years become terrain: green ridges, a long dry plain, and through the middle of it a ravine, dark and narrow.

script.text: ...That's the pit, isn't it. Those six years. From inside it felt like the whole map. It felt like the world had always been that and would always be that.
From ground level, a ravine is the horizon in every direction. From up here, observe: it is four hundred metres wide. And see the far wall — those small cuts, evenly spaced, going up?

You cut them. One per week, roughly — the walks you forced yourself to take, the one call you kept answering, the job you hated but held. Nobody lowered you a rope, Nils. You terraced your own way out and never once looked back to see the staircase. Fear keeps the eyes forward. That's its job. Altitude is the only place the staircase shows.
Show me why I'm really here. The threads. Everyone talks about the threads.

script.note: The overlay lights. Threads of gold rise off the terrain and arc outward — dozens, then hundreds, anchored in his years and landing in other lives.

script.text: Two hundred and fourteen threads, each one consented. This one: 2035, you taught a boy on Delta Row to patch a bicycle tube. He has taught eleven children since. The thread continues without you — that's what the branching means. This one: soup, four winters ago, a door you knocked on twice when once would have been polite. This small steady one: a joke you made in a queue in 2031. She still replays it on bad days. You have never learned her name.
I was *in* all those years. Why didn't I see any of this from the ground?

Because ground-level attention is a flashlight held by fear, and fear points it at problems. It's a good guard and a terrible historian. Nothing here was hidden, Nils. It was all simply behind you, and fear never once let you turn around. These are the things you didn't know you missed. From above, there is no behind.
There are also thirty-one grey marks. On the rim of the map. What are those?

Threads that exist, whose owners declined to be shown. I tell you the count because the count is also an answer: you mattered more widely than the permissions reach. And before you ask — there, the dark region, north-west. I show it because honesty is the room.
Anders. The friendship I burned down. Is there a dial for that? An overlay that fixes it?
No. The map does not advise, and repair is not a view — it's a walk. The Mend sits Thursdays. That is a fact about the town, not a suggestion about you.
One more question, and then bring me down. When I've gone — wherever I go — does this keep updating? The threads. Do they stop at the border?

Threads don't check the census. The boy will keep teaching. The joke will keep working. A life leaks light long after the person walks away from it — the only variable is whether you're somewhere that lets you see it happening. Descending now. Mind the ground; it always feels smaller than it did.

script.note: He leaves the room and turns left — not toward home. North-west. The next morning, the Threshold logs an amendment to one departure filing: 'permanent' has been crossed out, and the word written over it is 'a season'.
